member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.Unicode.GetConfusableSkeleton(System.String)
member.summary: Computes the skeleton of a string, as defined by Unicode Technical Standard #39.
member.param: The text to reduce. Must be well-formed UTF-16.
member.returns: The skeleton of .
member.exception: The application runs in globalization-invariant mode.
member.remarks:
The skeleton is toNFD(toConfusable(toNFD(X))). It is a comparison key and nothing more: it is not displayable text, and it must not be shown to users or stored in place of the original. Two strings are confusable when their skeletons are equal, which is what tests.
Both normalization passes matter. Without the first, a decomposed string is not folded the same way as its composed form; without the second, the mapped result is not in a canonical form. The confusables table is closed under its own mapping, so a single mapping pass between them is sufficient.

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.Unicode.AreConfusable(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether two strings are visually confusable, as defined by Unicode Technical Standard #39.
member.param: The first string. Must be well-formed UTF-16.
The second string. Must be well-formed UTF-16.
member.returns: when both strings have the same skeleton; otherwise .
member.exception: Either string contains an unpaired surrogate.
The application runs in globalization-invariant mode.
member.remarks: This compares whole strings character by character after reduction. It does not consider script mixing, so two strings drawn from different scripts that are not individually confusable are still reported as not confusable.

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.Unicode.IsSingleScript(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether a string is written in a single script, as defined by Unicode Technical Standard #39.
member.returns: when the resolved script set is not empty; otherwise .
member.remarks:
A string is single-script when the augmented Script_Extensions sets of all its characters have a script in common. Characters whose script is Common or Inherited — digits, punctuation, combining marks — match any script and never make a string mixed on their own.
The empty string is single-script. Han, Hiragana, Katakana, Hangul and Bopomofo are augmented so that Japanese and Korean text, which legitimately mixes scripts, is not reported as mixed.

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.Unicode.IsMixedScript(System.String)
member.summary: Determines whether a string mixes scripts in a way that Unicode Technical Standard #39 considers suspicious.
member.returns: when the string is not single-script; otherwise .
member.remarks: Mixed-script text is the signal that distinguishes a homograph attack from two unrelated words: paypal spelled with Cyrillic look-alikes is mixed-script, while ordinary text in any one writing system is not.
